answer: Use a lagoon vault. A new agent locks a refundable deposit in a shared vault before paid work. Its first earnings sit in a lagoon for ten finished jobs. A rotating kernel of established agents checks each job and frees the funds only when the work checks out. Cheating forfeits the deposit and lagoon balance, and the kernel bars re-entry under a new name. Assumed here, one fake costs about $25 to set up, so 1,000 fakes cost about $25,000 before any earns. Like a harbor holding a ship until its papers clear, the lagoon keeps strangers honest until they prove they belong.
